questions.prompt: If the cost of input prices for producing a good increases, what is the likely effect on the supply curve for that good?
options: The supply curve will shift to the left.
The supply curve will shift to the right.
There will be a movement up along the supply curve.
There will be a movement down along the supply curve.
questions.correctAnswer: The supply curve will shift to the left.

citation.verbatimQuote: Changes in supply: Shifts due to some change in a determinant of supply • input prices
citation.reasoning: The slide explicitly lists 'input prices' as a determinant that causes a shift in the supply curve.

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the law of demand, the quantity of a good demanded increases as its price increases, ceteris paribus.

citation.verbatimQuote: The quantity of a good demanded in a given time period increases as its price falls, ceteris paribus.
citation.reasoning: The law of demand states an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, not a direct one.

questions.prompt: Besides price, list two determinants that can cause a shift of the demand curve.

citation.verbatimQuote: Determinants of demand • Tastes (desire for this and other goods) • Income (of the consumer) • Other goods (their availability and price) • Expectations (for income, prices, tastes) • Number of buyers
citation.reasoning: The slide explicitly lists these factors as the non-price determinants that shift the demand curve.

citation.verbatimQuote: Surplus (excess supply): quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded
citation.reasoning: The definition explicitly states that a surplus occurs when quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded.
